scope: Language-neutral vectors; Python test setup is the first consumer. Schema PASS alone is not behavior, deployed-service, or installed-package proof.

degradation_rules.message: Over 1,024 UTF-8 bytes: cut at a character boundary so that the text plus a trailing U+2026 fits 1,024 bytes; set logging.truncated=true.
degradation_rules.string_field: Over 1,024 UTF-8 bytes (exception.stacktrace: 2,048): cut the same way; set logging.truncated=true.
degradation_rules.unknown_or_unsupported_field: Remove the field, keep the record; logging.dropped_field_count = number removed. Unsupported = not JSON-encodable, non-finite number, or a string that is not valid Unicode.
degradation_rules.record: Over 4,096 bytes: shorten exception.stacktrace by whole frames, then remove custom fields, largest encoded size first (ties: key name descending), each counted, until it fits.
degradation_rules.error: error.type = the error's type name; exception.stacktrace = one 'at <function> (<file basename>:<line>)' per frame, innermost first; never the error message or argument values. A caller-supplied value for either field wins. A caller value that breaks its field rule (error.type: 1-128 chars, no whitespace; exception.stacktrace: non-empty) is removed and counted, and the SDK value applies.
degradation_rules.drop: Only a record that cannot be serialised, breaks a base-field rule (empty or unformattable message, event without outcome), or still exceeds 4,096 bytes after the steps above is dropped and counted.

write_model.summary: One write model in every language (design review F2): the caller never waits on the output; a bounded queue feeds one background writer; a full queue drops and counts; a write error is counted and the writer continues; close drains until a deadline. An ERROR/FATAL line waits at most error_wait_ms for the writer, so the line logged just before a hard exit is not lost. A logger that never logs owns no writer thread.

cases.expect: the slowest log call returns within caller_budget_ms; queue_full >= lines - queue_capacity - 1; after the output is unblocked the queued lines are written
io_errors == 1; written == 2; later lines are still written
the next line starts on a new line; every complete line is valid JSON
close returns failure within close_timeout_ms + 500 ms; undelivered lines are counted
a child process created by fork writes through its own new writer; the parent's queue is not shared
an ERROR line logged just before a hard process exit (no close) is on the output; the call returns within error_wait_ms + 50 ms
creating loggers that never log starts no writer thread or goroutine

write_model.caller_budget_note: The slowest single call must stay under this. A blocked output makes a call wait as long as the output stays blocked (seconds); scheduler, GC and CPU-throttling pauses on shared CI runners and limited pods reach tens of milliseconds, so the bound keeps a 10x margin both ways.

drop_metric.summary: One drop metric in every language (design review R1): every line the SDK does not write is counted under one process-wide counter per (service, reason), readable as a snapshot, as Prometheus text, and as an OpenTelemetry asynchronous counter.
drop_metric.help: Log records the logging SDK did not write, by reason.

prometheus_text_example.text:
# HELP onenexus_log_records_dropped_total Log records the logging SDK did not write, by reason.
# TYPE onenexus_log_records_dropped_total counter
onenexus_log_records_dropped_total{service="q\"\\\n",reason="invalid"} 2
onenexus_log_records_dropped_total{service="svc-a",reason="closed"} 0
onenexus_log_records_dropped_total{service="svc-b",reason="queue_full"} 7

cases.expect: after one handler for service S is created and nothing is logged, the snapshot has exactly the four reasons for S, each 0

a record the contract rejects adds 1 to invalid; a write error adds 1 to io_errors; a line after close adds 1 to closed; a blocked output adds the overflow to queue_full; each equals the handler's own stats counter
two handlers with the same service report one row per reason whose count is the sum of both handlers' counters
handlers with different services report separate rows; a drop in one never changes the other
after close the service's rows remain and never decrease
rendering prometheus_text_example.counts gives exactly prometheus_text_example.text: HELP and TYPE first, rows sorted by service then reason, label values escaped (backslash, double quote, newline)
registering on a meter creates one asynchronous monotonic counter named otel_name with unit otel_unit; a collection yields one observation per snapshot row with attributes service and reason

field_registry.summary: One field registry (design review E1): the schema's x-field-registry decides, when a logger is configured, whether each allowed custom field name may be logged; at log time a custom value must be a flat scalar of its registered type.

rules.protected: A protected field (x-protected-fields) is never a custom field.
rules.format: Matches name_pattern (lowercase, '.' between namespaces, '_' between words, at most 5 segments) and has at most name_max_chars characters.
rules.registered_field: A name in fields is accepted, even inside a reserved namespace.
rules.reserved: Otherwise a name in a reserved namespace (logging.*, k8s.*) is rejected: only the SDK or the collector writes it.
rules.namespace: Otherwise the name must have 2+ segments and its first segment must be a registered namespace; a single-segment name that is not a registered field is rejected.
rules.too_many: More than max_custom_fields names is rejected.
rules.value: At log time a custom field value must be a string, a finite number, a boolean or null; an object or array is removed and counted in logging.dropped_field_count. A registered field's value must match its type (integer: a whole number, not a boolean; number: any finite number) or be null, else it is removed and counted.

field_registry.names_expansion: names is a list, or {prefix, count}: prefix + str(i) for i in 0..count-1, or {prefix, repeat, count}: one name, prefix + repeat × count.

error_fingerprint.rule: When the record has error.type: the first 16 lowercase hex digits of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of error.type followed, for each line of exception.stacktrace, by a newline and that line with a trailing ':<digits>)' replaced by ')'. Uses the record's error.type and exception.stacktrace after caller values apply and before the record is fitted, so fitting never changes it. Never from the message. Protected: a caller value is removed and counted.

emission_cases.expect: an ERROR logged with an error carries logging.error_fingerprint = the rule over its emitted error.type and exception.stacktrace
the same error from the same call site logged twice has one fingerprint
a record whose stack is shortened to fit 4,096 bytes keeps the fingerprint of the unshortened record
a caller logging.error_fingerprint is removed and counted (logging.dropped_field_count); the SDK value applies
a record without error.type has no logging.error_fingerprint
